title: 2026-11-25_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_54f
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised Linux system infected with the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activities, understand the backdoor's behavior, and gather evidence for further remediation.
outcomes: Identify suspicious services and their associated ports.
Analyze systemd timers and services for persistence mechanisms.
Investigate lateral movement activities and data exfiltration.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
This command will display all services, including inactive ones.

2. Filter for active services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
```
Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

3. Inspect the suspicious service:
```bash
systemctl status systemkernelservicedefender.service
```
This command provides detailed information about the service, including its description, execution command, and status.

4. Identify the service name:
From the output of the previous command, note the service name `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services, including inactive ones.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Filter the list of services to show only running services using `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Inspect the suspicious service in detail with `systemctl status <service_name>`.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the suspicious service configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service
```
This command displays the service unit file, which contains the configuration details.

2. Identify the port number:
Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service unit file. The port number is specified as an argument to the `ncat` command.

3. Verify the port with network listeners:
```bash
ss -tulnp
```
This command lists all network listeners and their associated processes. Confirm that the port identified in the service configuration is indeed being used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title

levels.title: Identify Lateral Movement Service
levels.content: Investigate the compromised host to identify the component responsible for transferring files to another host. Unusual file synchronization activity has been detected between systems in the environment.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

2. Inspect the suspicious service:
```bash
systemctl status payload-transfer.service
```
This command provides detailed information about the service, including its description, execution command, and status.

3. Identify the service name:
From the output of the previous command, note the service name `payload-transfer.service`.
